1 · Motivation

Same photographer, different roads

Photographer 1, Australia: timestamp overlay along the bottom

Photographer 2, USA: the same white bonnet

Photographer 3, Canada: same lens and framing, low horizon

The road changes. The camera does not.

Most photographers drive in one country, so in training their camera alone predicts the label: a shortcut.

Research question

How much of a CNN’s accuracy survives for photographers it has never seen?

Photos: OSV-5M / Mapillary, CC BY-SA 4.0

∂L/∂zᵢ = pᵢ − yᵢ

The gradient for each score: Switzerland gets +0.56, so its score is pushed down; Austria gets 0.31 − 1 = −0.69, so its score is pushed up. Backpropagation carries this signal through all 11.2M weights.

h: the 512 pooled features · W: 32 × 512 weights · yᵢ = 1 for the true country, 0 otherwise · x-axis: probability given to the true country

Fingerprint removal

Original

What the network sees in training

Blank the bottom 20%

filled with the ImageNet mean colour, so the geometry stays the same

Re-encode as JPEG

at a random quality from 30 to 95

Jitter the colours

white balance ±15%; brightness, contrast and saturation ±25%

Keep the hue

road-marking colours are country cues

3 · Method

How we measure

Balanced accuracy

BA = mean recall over the 32 countries

Chance is 1/32 = 3.1%. With 400 test photos per country it equals plain accuracy.

Photographer gap

Δ = BA(seen) − BA(unseen)

Same model, same countries: only whether the photographer was in training differs.

Uncertainty

Resample photographers, not photos

A photographer’s photos move together. Paired draws compare two models on the same people.

Excess accuracy, used to explain the gap

E(B) = average over the photos in group B of ( correct − accuracy of its country on unseen photographers )

Above zero: the model does better on these seen photographers than on new photographers from the same countries.

95% intervals from 1,000 photographer-level bootstrap draws (Field and Welsh, 2007)

15

5 · Discussion

What the results mean

Countries are learned

31.9% on photographers it never saw, ten times chance. Its errors respect driving side and world region.

Photographers are learned too

+5.2 pp on familiar photographers. Absent in frozen features, it grows with exposure and is strongest within 25 km.

More of the same data is not the cure

261k extra photos gave +2.0 pp on unseen but +3.5 pp on seen photographers. Grow photographers, not photos.

Removing the camera has a price

The gap shrinks by 40%, but accuracy drops 3.6 pp: camera cues and road cues share the same pixels.

Learning Where

23

5 · Discussion

Limitations and ethics

Limitations

  • One seed and one split per model
  • End-to-end runs trained for only 6 epochs
  • At 128×170 px, signs and plates are unreadable
  • Removal changes three things at once
  • Per-country and exposure analyses are exploratory

Ethics

10–16%

same-photographer pairs that are nearest neighbours

0.1%

by chance

  • Features could link anonymous uploads to one vehicle and, with GPS, to where someone drives
  • Requiring 200 photographers leaves out almost all of Africa

Learning Where

24

Conclusion

A CNN learns countries from street photos, but part of its accuracy comes from recognising the photographers.

Evaluate

Report photographer-disjoint accuracy next to the official split

Collect

Grow the number of photographers, not photos per photographer
